criterion_notes.c1: Fails Criterion 1 (and falls under Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). The study examines upstream inter-basin bulk raw-water resource governance (governança das águas under Brazil's National Water Resources Policy, Lei n. 9.433/1997, SGIB, CBHSF, and Codevasf) in the São Francisco River Integration Project (PISF), which transfers raw river water to strategic state reservoirs. Contextual remarks that municipal water-supply infrastructure in Semiárido towns is obsolete or that water access in the region favours wealthier localities are background/infrastructural observations rather than an empirical investigation of household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, this study PASSES Criterion 2 because it analyses legal, institutional and governance arrangements (Lei n. 9.433/1997, Decreto n. 5.995/2006 creating SGIB, CBHSF, CNRH, Codevasf, inter-federative coordination, participatory asymmetries and Ostrom's IAD rules-in-use); however, plain_criterion2_decision remains 'exclude' because the paper still fails Criteria 1 and 4 as an upstream water-resource governance study rather than a household/community service-access study. Under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading, it FAILS Criterion 2: its focus is macro-level river-basin and megaproject governance (federal-state voting dominance in SGIB and CNRH/CBHSF, agency fragmentation and indigenous exclusion from decision arenas) rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access. Its brief mentions of tariffs/cost recovery and fragile boundary/enforcement rules apply to bulk raw-water pumping fees paid by states and irrigators to the federal canal operator and diffuse raw-water withdrawals along open canals crossing private lands, not rules governing household or community water/sanitation utility service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Satisfies Criterion 3. Qualitative empirical institutional case study derived from a doctoral dissertation, combining documentary analysis (EIA, water legislation, CGU/TCU audit reports) and primary open/conversational individual interviews conducted between 2015 and 2018 (recorded, transcribed and analysed in NVivo 11) with federal/state officials, researchers and quilombola and indigenous community representatives.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4. The empirically analysed outcomes are macro-governance and socio-environmental processes in the PISF action arena—centralised decision-making in SGIB and CNRH/CBHSF, power and information asymmetries, silencing of indigenous (Pipipã) and quilombola voices in governance forums, inter-agency overlap, and destruction of 1,250 km² of native Caatinga—rather than household or community water or sanitation service-access outcomes (such as connection, utility service availability, household affordability or disconnection).
criterion_notes.c5: Within its water-resources governance scope, the paper provides enough information to identify the study design (qualitative institutional case study using Ostrom's IAD framework), unit of analysis (the PISF regional water-governance action arena in Pernambuco and interviewed actor groups), institutional governance exposure and institutional/socio-environmental outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: Este estudo busca compreender a gestão complexa da água analisando o sistema de governança das águas na área de influência do Projeto de Integração do Rio São Francisco (PISF), utilizando o Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) Framework de Elinor Ostrom para observância de fatores exógenos, situação de ação e interações e resultados.

Este estudo adota uma abordagem metodológica de natureza qualitativa (Godoi & Balsini, 2010), e a coleta de dados foi realizada entre os anos de 2015 e 2018, conforme a realização de entrevistas em formato conversacional, livre e padronizado aberto, com o objetivo de compreender os significados atribuídos aos problemas da governança da água (Creswell, 2010).

Na esfera estadual, os estados partícipes do PISF — Pernambuco, Paraíba, Rio Grande do Norte e Ceará — cobram as tarifas de serviços, operação, manutenção e direito de uso da água. A regulação dos usuários autorizados a bombear a água transposta está condicionada ao pagamento à operadora nacional pelos custos de operação e manutenção

Dessa forma, a transposição conduz volumes adequados de água para os reservatórios estratégicos estaduais, sendo distribuída para as demais estruturas de abastecimento hídrico. No entanto, a ausência de manutenção dessas estruturas secundárias compromete os investimentos no projeto, uma vez que os eixos da transposição dependem da infraestrutura existente para garantir a chegada das águas aos consumidores finais.

Em relação à arena de ação, os atores estatais detêm papel central, mas há assimetria de poder e de informação em relação às organizações locais, comunidades indígenas e quilombolas, e associações civis. A participação é prevista formalmente, porém, na prática, prevalece a centralização decisória da União e estados.

raw_response.exposure: Macro-level water-resources institutional governance arrangements of the PISF inter-basin water transfer (Lei n. 9.433/1997, SGIB, CBHSF, CNRH, Codevasf, bulk raw-water pumping charges and canal oversight) analysed via Ostrom's IAD framework
raw_response.outcome: Institutional governance and socio-environmental outcomes in the PISF action arena: federal-state centralization in SGIB/CNRH, inter-agency fragmentation, power and information asymmetries, political exclusion of indigenous and quilombola communities, strategic reservoir degradation and clearing of 1,250 km² of native Caatinga
raw_response.population_and_sample: Unit of analysis: institutional action arena of the São Francisco River Integration Project (PISF) in Pernambuco (Agreste and Sertão, North and East Axes). Qualitative sample (2015–2018): documentary corpus (EIA, legislation, CGU/TCU reports) plus individual interviews with representatives of MI, APAC/Prorural, Fundaj, Observatório das Águas (OGA), Compesa, Codevasf, one quilombola community in Garanhuns and two indigenous communities (including Pipipã) in Ibimirim and Pesqueira.
raw_response.rationale: Exclude (E01 - Wrong topic; Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource study unrelated to household or community service access). Although this is a primary qualitative empirical study (documentary analysis and interviews conducted 2015–2018) in Portuguese, its object of analysis is upstream inter-basin bulk raw-water resource governance (governança das águas under Brazil's National Water Resources Policy, Lei n. 9.433/1997, SGIB, CBHSF, CNRH and Codevasf) in the São Francisco River transposition megaproject (PISF), not household or community drinking-water or sanitation service access (c1 = no). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading of Criterion 2, it also fails c2 because it analyses macro-level collegiate river-basin/project governance and bulk raw-water pumping fees/canal oversight rather than rule-type mechanisms directly governing household or community service access. Its empirical findings concern participatory power/information asymmetries, inter-governmental fragmentation, secondary reservoir obsolescence and native Caatinga loss/cultural conflict rather than household or community service-access outcomes (c4 = no). Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2 (where macro water governance satisfies c2), the study remains excluded for failing Criteria 1 and 4.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative empirical institutional case study (documentary research and individual open/conversational interviews analysed with NVivo 11 using Ostrom's IAD framework)
